mainTopic: How an אלמנה sells her husband's property, whether a sale made for a need that falls away is undone, and when a widow must sell through בית דין.
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier comparison: someone collecting is better off calling what he takes a debt payment, not a gift. The גמרא then asks how an אלמנה sells property for her food. רב הונא says she sells once every twelve months, רב יהודה says once every six months, and in both views the buyer pays her every thirty days. אמימר rules like רב יהודה. Next, רב ששת is asked whether a widow who sold land for her מזונות can later seize it back for her כתובה. He proves from a ברייתא, read carefully, that she cannot: she may collect only from what she left unsold. The גמרא then asks whether a sale is undone if the seller ends up not needing the money. After two proofs are pushed aside, it rules that such a sale is undone. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a widow may sell without בית דין, while רבי שמעון requires בית דין for a widow from אירוסין. The גמרא begins to question the first opinion's ruling about her, and its answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A gift gives a weaker claim than a debt
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of an earlier comparison: someone who takes property as a gift has a weaker claim than someone who takes it as payment of a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he takes it as a gift, his power is not as strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an argument from the previous section. Someone owed both a debt and a gift is better off saying he is taking the property for the debt, because calling it a gift would leave him in a weaker position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A debt gives the creditor a stronger claim than a gift does. The earlier passage used this idea as a comparison: just as he may choose to call it the stronger kind of claim, an אלמנה can decide after the sale which purpose her sale was for.

keyTerms.meaning: His power or claim is strong

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an earlier discussion, not the start of a new topic. The new topic begins with the next step, כיצד מוכרת.

phrases.english: If he takes them as a gift,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the properties he is collecting.

phrases.english: his power is not as strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם בְּמַתָּנָה נוֹטְלָן לֹא כָּךְ יָפֶה כֹּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the comparison from the preceding passage on the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Calling it a gift weakens his claim, so he would choose to say he is collecting a debt. The comparison supports letting the אלמנה decide her purpose afterward.

steps.title: How does the widow sell?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question about the practical process of an אלמנה selling property for her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does she sell?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how, in practice, an אלמנה sells her husband's property to pay for her food. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know she may sell for her מזונות. The open question is the method: how often she sells, and how she gets the money.

phrases.english: How does she sell?
phrases.notes: "She" is the אלמנה, selling to pay for her food and support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The procedure and timing of the widow's sale of property for her support.

steps.title: רב הונא: sell once a year, paid monthly
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says she sells once for twelve months' worth of support, and the buyer pays her every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דניאל בר רב קטינא said in the name of רב הונא: She sells once for twelve months, and the buyer supports her once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first answer. She makes one sale that covers a full year, and the buyer pays her the money in monthly portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to this answer. The sale itself happens only once a year. The money reaches her a month at a time, from the buyer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי דָּנִיאֵל בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Daniel bar Rav Ketina said
that Rav Huna said:
She sells once for twelve months,
and the buyer provides for her once every thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי דָּנִיאֵל בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She sells once a year, and the buyer pays her monthly.

steps.title: רב יהודה: sell every six months, paid monthly
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says she sells once for six months' worth of support, and the buyer still pays monthly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: She sells for six months, and the buyer supports her once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a second answer. He disagrees only about how often she sells.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that the buyer pays her every thirty days. The only disagreement is whether each sale covers twelve months or six.
steps.confusionAlert: The two views do not argue about the monthly payments. They argue only about how long each sale covers.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
She sells for six months,
and the buyer provides for her once every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא about how often she sells.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She sells every six months, and the buyer pays her monthly.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רב הונא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רב הונא: She sells for twelve months, and the buyer supports her once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says exactly what רב הונא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רב הונא's view backing from an older source. It is not a challenge to anyone; it simply shows he has support.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Huna:
She sells for twelve months,
and the buyer provides for her once every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view in step 3.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא is quoted that matches רב יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רב יהודה: She sells for six months, and the buyer supports her once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה also has a ברייתא supporting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side now has an older source behind it. So the ברייתות alone cannot settle the argument, and a ruling is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
She sells for six months,
and the buyer provides for her once every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other view matching support.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: אמימר rules like רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that the הלכה is six months, following רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that she sells for six months, and the buyer supports her once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר settles the argument and rules like רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both views had a ברייתא behind them, a ruling was needed. אמימר picks the six-month approach.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for how an אלמנה sells for her support.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halakha is:
She sells for six months
and the buyer provides for her once every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב יהודה: she sells every six months and is paid monthly.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר what he makes of רב הונא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What about רב הונא's view?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks why אמימר ignored רב הונא, who also had a ברייתא supporting him. This question sets up אמימר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's view was backed by a ברייתא too. So רב אשי wants to know why it was not chosen, or whether אמימר simply did not know about it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What about that of Rav Huna?
phrases.notes: This is asking about רב הונא's twelve-month view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר דְּרַב הוּנָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ruling in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אמימר did not rule like רב הונא.

steps.title: I don't hold like it
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he "did not hear" רב הונא's view, meaning he does not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear it, meaning: I do not hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר explains that saying "I didn't hear it" is his way of saying he rejects that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase sounds as if he was unaware of רב הונא's view, but the גמרא explains its real meaning: "I do not agree with it." So the ruling stays like רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not hold this view

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: an אלמנה sells once every six months, and the buyer pays her every thirty days. אמימר rejects רב הונא's twelve-month view.
steps.confusionAlert: "I did not hear it" does not mean he never knew about the view. Here it is a polite way of saying "I disagree."

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not hear it,
that is to say: I do not hold like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי כְּלוֹמַר לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר does not hold like רב הונא, so his ruling for רב יהודה stands.

steps.title: Can a widow take back what she sold for food?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is asked whether a widow who sold property for her מזונות can later seize that same property for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: if a widow sells property to pay for her food, may she go back and seize that same property as payment for her כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is put to רב ששת. A widow sold land to support herself; can she later take that land back from the buyer to collect her כתובה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow has two separate rights: her daily מזונות, and her כתובה payment. Here she used the first right to sell land. The question is whether she can then use the second right to pull that very land back from the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him, raising a question they could not settle
Food and support a widow gets from her late husband's property
The sum a wife collects when her marriage ends
To seize property from a buyer to collect a debt

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:
A woman who sells property for her food,
may she go back and seize it for her marriage contract?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a widow selling for מזונות, after אמימר's ruling closed the earlier discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a widow who sold land for מזונות later seize that same land from the buyer for her כתובה?

steps.title: The background: רב יוסף's rule about the guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question is built on רב יוסף's rule: when a widow or a court sells, the guarantee falls on the orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked this because of רב יוסף's rule. רב יוסף said: when a widow sells, the guarantee is on the orphans; and when a court sells, the guarantee is on the orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give the background rule that makes the question possible. This line is setting up the two sides of the question that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a seller guarantees the buyer: if the land is taken away, the seller pays him back. רב יוסף says a widow is different. She sells for the estate, so the יתומים carry that guarantee, not her. That is why someone might think she is free to take the land back herself.

keyTerms.meaning: They were asking this in connection with
A guarantee to the buyer: if the land is taken, he gets paid back

phrases.english: They asked this in light of Rav Yosef's rule.
For Rav Yosef said:
When a widow sells, the guarantee is on the orphans,
phrases.notes: If a creditor later takes the land from the buyer, the orphans must pay the buyer back, not the widow.

phrases.english: and when a court sells, the guarantee is on the orphans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background rule behind the question in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a widow or a court sells the deceased's property, the יתומים carry the אחריות, not the seller.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Since the guarantee is on the orphans, maybe she can seize the land. Or maybe the buyers can say she at least promised not to take it back herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the law? Since the guarantee is on the orphans, can she seize it? Or perhaps the buyers can tell her: 'True, you did not promise to protect us from everyone else. But didn't you at least promise that you yourself would not take it back?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out both sides of the question. Either she may seize the land because she gave no guarantee, or she may not because she at least promised not to take it back herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: she carries no guarantee, so nothing stops her from seizing the land. Side two splits the guarantee into two parts. One part protects the buyer from other people, and she did not take that on. The other part promises that the seller herself will not come back for the land, and every seller takes that on.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; brings in the other side of a question
Granted that; admits one point before making another
A guarantee against anyone else taking the land
A guarantee that you yourself will not take it back

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of guarantee. רב יוסף only freed her from the guarantee against other people. The question is whether she still promised not to take the land back herself.

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since the guarantee is on the orphans, she may seize it,
or perhaps the buyers can say to her:
Granted that a guarantee against everyone else
you did not take upon yourself,
but a guarantee about your own actions
did you not surely take on?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּאַחְרָיוּת אַיַּתְמֵי, טָרְפָא, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב יוסף's rule from step 11 to lay out both sides of the question from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does being free of the general guarantee also let her take the land back, or did she still promise that she herself would not take it?

steps.title: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא: she cannot take it back
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא: a widow sells only until her כתובה's value is left, and she collects from that remainder. So she cannot seize what she already sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: you learned it in a ברייתא: 'She keeps selling until only the value of her כתובה is left, and she relies on collecting her כתובה from what remains.' Learn from this: if she left enough, yes, she can collect. If she did not leave enough, no, she cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers with a ברייתא. A widow must leave enough property to cover her כתובה, which shows she cannot take back land she already sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she could seize sold land for her כתובה, she would never need to stop selling. She could sell everything and then take some back. The ברייתא tells her to stop and save a remainder for her כתובה. So the sold land is closed to her, and the second side of step 12 wins: she did promise not to take it back herself.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it, in a ברייתא
Learn from this; draws a conclusion from a source

steps.whatToRemember: A widow who sold land for her מזונות cannot later seize that land for her כתובה. She can only collect her כתובה from property she left unsold.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a seller who carries no general guarantee still cannot take back what she herself sold.

phrases.english: He said to him: you learned it:
She keeps selling until only the value of her marriage contract is left,

phrases.aramaic: וְסֶמֶךְ לָהּ שֶׁתִּגְבֶּה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מִן הַשְּׁאָר.
phrases.english: and she relies on collecting her marriage contract from the remainder.
Learn from this:
If she left some over, yes, she collects,
if she did not leave some over, no.
phrases.notes: He means she cannot fall back on taking the sold land from the buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from steps 10–12 with a ברייתא and an inference from it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. She can only collect her כתובה from property she left unsold, not from land she already sold.
steps.raayaObject: That a widow cannot seize land she sold for מזונות to collect her כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: she sells only until the value of her כתובה is left and collects from the remainder.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא is only giving good advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's proof. Perhaps the ברייתא is only advising the widow to avoid a bad reputation, not stating the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the ברייתא is just giving good advice, so that people won't call her a 'retractor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 13. It suggests the ברייתא may be practical advice, not a legal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 read the ברייתא as saying she legally cannot seize what she sold. This step offers another reading: she could legally take it back, but she shouldn't, because people would call her untrustworthy. If that is right, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Good advice, not a strict legal rule
A woman who goes back on her deals (a 'retractor')

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: But perhaps it is teaching us good advice,
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא that רב ששת just quoted.

phrases.english: so that they will not call her a "retractor."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב ששת brought in step 13 by reading the ברייתא as advice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not the conclusion itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be practical advice about her reputation rather than a legal limit on her rights.

steps.title: The words ״סמך לה״ show it is a real law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'good advice' reading. If it were only advice, the ברייתא would simply say she collects from the remainder. The extra word ״סמך לה״ shows she may collect only from what is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the ברייתא should just say 'she collects her כתובה from the remainder.' Why does it say 'she relies on it'? Learn from this: if she left something over, yes, she collects; if she left nothing, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 14 by looking closely at the ברייתא's wording. This brings back רב ששת's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain advice would only need the words 'she collects from the remainder.' The ברייתא's choice of ״סמך לה״, that the remainder is what she leans on, means the remainder is her only source. So if she sold everything, she has nothing to collect from, and she cannot seize what she sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach, meaning 'then it should have said'
Her support, what she relies on

steps.whatToRemember: A widow who sold land for her מזונות can collect her כתובה only from what she left unsold. She cannot seize the land she already sold.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach:
"She collects her marriage contract from the remainder,"
Why does it say "she relies on it"?
phrases.notes: These are the ברייתא's actual words from step 13: the remainder is what she leans on.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
If she left some over, yes, she collects;
if she did not leave any over, no, she does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defeats the 'good advice' rejection in step 14 by pointing to precise wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the source's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might only be advising her to protect her reputation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording ״סמך לה״ makes it a legal limit: she collects only from what remains.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She cannot seize the property she sold for her מזונות.

steps.title: Is a sale undone if the seller ends up not needing the money?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: someone sold property because he needed money, and in the end he did not need it. Is the sale undone or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone sold, and then did not need the money, is the sale reversed or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks whether a sale made for a specific need falls apart when that need disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: the seller only sold because of the need, so the sale was based on a mistake and can be undone. Other side: a sale is a sale, and the seller's private reason does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If he sold, and then he did not need the money,
is the sale reversed,
or is the sale not reversed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the widow discussion closed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a sale made for a need that later disappears can be cancelled.

steps.title: Proof from רב פפא returning a field
steps.stepSummary: A man sold land to רב פפא to buy oxen. In the end he did not need the money, and רב פפא gave him back the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a man sold land to רב פפא because he needed money to buy oxen. In the end he didn't need it, and רב פפא returned his land to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as a possible answer to the question in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא returned the land once the seller's need was gone. That suggests the sale is undone when the need disappears.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין אַרְעָא לְרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold land to Rav Pappa
because he needed money to buy oxen.
In the end he did not need it,
and Rav Pappa returned his land to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the sale is reversed when the need for money falls away.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב פפא returning the land.

steps.title: רב פפא went beyond the law
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רב פפא returned the land out of extra kindness, not because the law required it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא acted beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act done לפנים משורת הדין, going further than the law demands, tells us nothing about what the law itself is. So this story does not settle the question from step 16. Step 24 gives the final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond the letter of the law, doing more than required

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין הוּא דַּעֲבַד.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa acted beyond the letter of the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רב פפא's story.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question is settled later, in step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא's act was extra kindness, not a ruling of law.

steps.title: Proof from the drought in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: During a drought in נהרדעא, everyone sold their mansions to buy food. Then wheat arrived, and רב נחמן ruled that the law is that the mansions go back to their owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: there was a drought in נהרדעא, and everyone sold their mansions. In the end wheat arrived. רב נחמן told them: the law is that the mansions return to their owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for the question in step 16, this time a legal ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב פפא's story, רב נחמן says outright ״דינא הוא״, 'this is the law.' So this cannot be brushed off as extra kindness. It seems to show that a sale made because of a need is undone when the need disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the law (not just kindness)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There was a certain drought in Neharde'a,
and everyone sold their mansions,
In the end, wheat arrived.
Rav Nachman said to them:
The law is that the mansions go back to their owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּהָהוּא בִּצּוּרְתָּא דַּהֲוָת בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a second and stronger proof is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That a sale made for a need is reversed when the need disappears.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling in נהרדעא, stated as ״דינא הוא״.

steps.title: The drought sale was a mistake from the start
steps.stepSummary: The proof from נהרדעא is rejected. The wheat ship was already nearby when the mansions were sold, so the sale was a mistaken sale from the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, the sales were a mistake, because it later came out that the ship was already standing in the bends of the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 19. It says the drought case does not prove our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our question is about a sale that was fine when it was made, where things only changed later. In נהרדעא the wheat ship was already close when people sold, so the sale was flawed from the very start. That is a מקח טעות, a different case, so it proves nothing about our question.

keyTerms.meaning: It came out later, it was revealed
Bends or bays of the river

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the difference: a sale that was wrong from the start (the ship was already near) is not the same as a sale that was fine but later became pointless. Our question is only about the second kind.

phrases.english: There too:
phrases.notes: "There" means the נהרדעא drought case from the last step.

phrases.english: the sales were made in error,
since it was revealed
that the ship was already standing in the bends of the river.
phrases.notes: So the food was already almost there when they sold. They just didn't know it yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the נהרדעא ruling as proof for a sale that only became unnecessary later.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נהרדעא sale was a mistake at the time of sale, because the ship was already close. Our question is about circumstances that changed after the sale.

steps.title: Support from רמי בר שמואל's challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading: that explains why רמי בר שמואל challenged רב נחמן, saying his ruling would make trouble for buyers in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is why רמי בר שמואל said to רב נחמן: If this is the rule, you will be tripping people up in the future!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new reading by pointing to a conversation between רמי בר שמואל and רב נחמן. This step opens that conversation, and the next steps finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר שמואל worried that after every drought, buyers would lose their land, so people would stop buying. This conversation is used to show that רב נחמן's ruling was tied to the special drought case, and was not a general rule for every sale.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what he said to him; that explains his words
You make them stumble, you cause them trouble

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the drought sale really was a special mistake case.

phrases.english: this is what he said to him,
Rami bar Shmuel to Rav Naḥman:
If so,
you end up tripping them up for the future!
phrases.notes: "Them" means future buyers. They won't want to buy land if sales can be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of step 20 by pointing to a recorded conversation.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן's ruling was tied to the special drought case and was not a general rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exchange between רמי בר שמואל and רב נחמן about future harm to buyers.

steps.title: רב נחמן: droughts are not an everyday thing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that his ruling will not cause wide harm, because a drought does not happen every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is a drought something that happens every day?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling against רמי בר שמואל's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן limits his ruling to the drought situation. Since droughts are rare, buyers will not often lose land. This shows his ruling was about a special case, which fits the reading in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question that expects "no")

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is the one answering here.

phrases.english: Is it as if every day
a drought is common?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ כׇּל יוֹמָא בִּצּוּרְתָּא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר שמואל's challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a rare situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רמי בר שמואל thought the ruling would harm buyers all the time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling only applies in a drought, which is rare, so the harm is small.

steps.title: רמי בר שמואל: in נהרדעא droughts are common
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר שמואל answers back that in נהרדעא droughts happen often, so the worry is real.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, in נהרדעא drought is very common.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר שמואל pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. This ends their conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said droughts are rare. רמי בר שמואל says that is not true in נהרדעא, where they happen often. So in his view, the ruling could still make people afraid to buy land there.

keyTerms.meaning: Very common, happens all the time

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: Now רמי בר שמואל is speaking again.

phrases.english: drought in Neharde'a
is very common.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, בִּצּוּרְתָּא בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא מִשְׁכָּח שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that droughts are rare.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In נהרדעא droughts are frequent, so the ruling would often undo sales and scare buyers away.

steps.title: The final הלכה: the sale is undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules: if someone sold for a purpose and then did not need the money, the sale goes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if he sold and then did not need the money, the sale is reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the question from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the proofs were each pushed away, the גמרא decides that the sale is undone. The seller clearly sold only for a certain need, so once that need is gone, the sale does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The sale goes back, it is undone

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: if someone sold property because he needed money for something, and in the end he did not need it, the sale is undone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the open question from step 16 and gives a practical rule about sales made for a stated purpose.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
if he sold, and he did not end up needing the money —
the sale is reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: זַבֵּין וְלָא אִיצְטְרִיכוּ לֵיהּ זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole discussion that began in step 16 with a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale made for a specific need is undone if that need never came about.

steps.title: New משנה: a widow may sell without בית דין
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: an אלמנה, whether widowed after אירוסין or after נישואין, may sell her late husband's property without going to בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A widow, whether from betrothal or from marriage, may sell without a court.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It is about how a widow collects what she is owed from her husband's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the widow can sell property herself, without asking בית דין. This holds whether she was only engaged (אירוסין) or fully married (נישואין) when her husband died.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A widow, whether from betrothal
or from marriage —
sells when not in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין מִן הָאֵירוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow, whether widowed after אירוסין or after נישואין, may sell her late husband's property without בית דין.

steps.title: רבי שמעון splits the widow cases by whether she receives food support
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה. A widow from נישואין may sell without בית דין. A widow from אירוסין may sell only in בית דין, because she gets no מזונות. He adds a general rule: anyone without מזונות sells only in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: a widow from marriage may sell without בית דין. A widow from betrothal may sell only in בית דין, because she does not receive food support. Anyone who does not receive food support may sell only in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion, from רבי שמעון. He does not let every widow sell on her own the way the first opinion did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה (step 25) let both kinds of widow sell without בית דין. רבי שמעון makes the rule depend on מזונות. A widow who is supported from her husband's estate may sell on her own, but a widow who is not supported must go through בית דין. He then states this as a general rule for anyone in that situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Food support. A widow from marriage is supported from her late husband's estate.
Full marriage, the final stage of marriage
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage, before living together
Rabbinic court that oversees the sale
Not in court, meaning on her own

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. The first opinion lets BOTH widows sell without בית דין. Only רבי שמעון sends the widow from אירוסין to court.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין מוֹכֶרֶת שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: A widow from marriage sells when not in court,
but a widow from betrothal may not sell
except in court,
because she does not receive sustenance.
And anyone who does not receive sustenance
may sell only in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same משנה that disagrees with the first opinion in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow from נישואין sells without בית דין. A widow from אירוסין, or anyone without מזונות, sells only in בית דין.

steps.title: Granted: the married widow sells without בית דין because of her food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the first opinion of the משנה. It grants that a widow from נישואין may sell without בית דין because she needs food now and should not have to wait. This sets up the question of why the first opinion also lets a widow from אירוסין sell without בית דין, when she gets no מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא says: granted, a widow from marriage may sell without בית דין, because of her food needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a 'בשלמא' line. It grants the reason for the widow from נישואין, so that it can next ask why the first opinion of the משנה lets a widow from אירוסין sell without בית דין too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow from נישואין is supported from the estate and has to eat now, so she cannot be made to wait until she finds a בית דין to oversee the sale. But a widow from אירוסין gets no מזונות, so that reason does not apply to her. Why, then, does the first opinion let her sell without בית דין? The גמרא's answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
'Granted' or 'It makes sense'. It opens a two-part challenge: this part is fine, but the other part is hard.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, a widow from marriage may sell when not in court
because of her sustenance,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts analyzing the first opinion of the משנה from step 25, which, unlike רבי שמעון in step 26, lets even the betrothed widow sell without בית דין
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion of the משנה (תנא קמא), which lets a widow from אירוסין sell without בית דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the married widow's case is explained by her urgent need for food. A betrothed widow gets no מזונות, so the next line will ask why the first opinion lets her sell without בית דין.
